title: 3-Read Friday #87: Personalisation, Teaching with AI, and Today's Parents
author: Craig Barton
summary: 3-Read Friday #87 is dominated by AI's promises and limits. Becky Allen examines what AI-driven personalisation means for the future of learning, which Barton flags as a "blistering post" from one of the country's leading assessment experts. Dominic Salles then shares a specific, practical use of NotebookLM -- Barton's self-declared favourite free AI tool -- for lesson planning. Andrew Old closes the issue away from AI, arguing that a genuine minority of ideologically motivated parents, shaped by their own 2000s schooling under a "blamelessness" philosophy, are driving today's most difficult parent-school conflicts. Barton also flags Book 5 of his Tips for Teachers series, on Checking for Listening.
points: Allen's piece is framed by Barton as unusually forceful ("blistering") for an assessment specialist writing about AI's implications for personalised learning.

Salles' NotebookLM walkthrough is offered by Barton as a direct extension of his own long-running enthusiasm for the tool, positioning it as one concrete, adoptable classroom use case rather than abstract AI commentary.

Old's piece is the issue's outlier, moving away from AI to argue that a genuinely ideologically distinct minority of parents -- shaped by their own 2000s "blamelessness" schooling -- now drives a disproportionate share of school-parent conflict.
The issue closes on Barton's own publishing note (Book 5 of Tips for Teachers, on Checking for Listening), tying the newsletter's practical throughline back to his own writing project.
quotes: A blistering post on AI and what it means for the future of personalised learning by one of the leading assessment experts in the country.
Long-time readers will know I am officially the world’s biggest NotebookLM fan. Here, Dominic shares a really smart use of the free tool to aid lesson planning.

Andrew makes a compelling case that the attitudes of many of today’s parents towards behaviour are influenced by their own experiences of school in the 2000s, which may have had different expectations of schools today.
Before we begin, you may want to check out my brand-new 16-part book series, The Tips for Teachers guide to. Book 5 on Checking for Listening is now available.
